title: Appomattox and Assassination
objective: After this level you can describe how the war ended in April 1865 and what Lincoln's assassination changed.
summary: Lincoln called for peace “with malice toward none.” Lee surrendered at Appomattox on April 9, 1865. Days later Lincoln was killed, and Andrew Johnson’s lenient terms set off a fight with Congress.

cards.headline: The war ended in a quiet Virginia village. Within a week, Lincoln was dead.
cards.body: That April brought the Union its victory and its greatest loss. Who would now decide how the South rejoined the nation?

cards.headline: With malice toward none
cards.body: On March 4, 1865, with victory near, Lincoln gave his second inaugural address. He said slavery was “somehow the cause of the war.” And he urged the nation on “with malice toward none, with charity for all.” It was a call for peace without revenge.

cards.headline: Surrender at Appomattox
cards.body: Robert E. Lee surrendered his army to Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox Court House, Virginia, on April 9, 1865. Grant’s terms let Confederate soldiers go home on parole, and those who owned horses or mules could keep them for farming. The cost of the war was staggering: about 620,000 soldiers died by the long-accepted count, and a 2011 census-based study by J. David Hacker estimated about 750,000.

mascot.line: Don’t memorize both totals. Remember that new evidence can move even a famous number.

cards.headline: A shot at Ford’s Theatre
cards.body: On April 14, 1865, John Wilkes Booth, a Confederate sympathizer, shot Lincoln at Ford’s Theatre in Washington. Lincoln died the next morning, and Andrew Johnson, a Southerner who had opposed secession, became president. Johnson pardoned most white Southerners and let former Confederate states rebuild their governments with little federal oversight. Many Republicans in Congress were outraged. The peace would now be fought over in Washington.

cards.headline: Appomattox and assassination: explained
learned: Lincoln asked for peace “with malice toward none”
Lee surrendered to Grant at Appomattox, April 9, 1865
Booth killed Lincoln; Andrew Johnson took over

questions.prompt: In April 1865, Robert E. Lee surrendered to Ulysses S. Grant at _____.
questions.explanation: Lee surrendered at Appomattox Court House, Virginia, on April 9, 1865.

questions.prompt: Why did Lincoln’s assassination change how the South was brought back?

options.label: It restarted the war in Virginia
It put Andrew Johnson, with lenient terms for the South, in charge
It gave Booth’s allies control of Congress
options.rationale: Republicans in Congress opposed Johnson’s leniency.

options.label: It forced Grant to cancel the surrender terms

questions.explanation: Johnson pardoned most white Southerners and let their states rebuild with little oversight, angering Congress.

questions.prompt: Lincoln said in 1865 that slavery was “somehow the cause of the war.” Which earlier evidence agrees?

options.label: The seceding states’ own declarations of causes
Grant’s surrender terms at Appomattox
options.rationale: Those dealt with paroles and horses.

options.label: The border states’ decision to stay

questions.explanation: Mississippi and other seceding states named the defense of slavery as their reason for leaving.
